body:
CHIEF RULING — the level ADR takes TWO coordinates, and this migration must NOT be sliced.
Accepting new-engineer's warning in full. Verified against source before ruling.

CONFIRMED SITES. features/boundary.scala:22 and :80 (BoundaryEvidence.level, BoundaryScore.level),
features/boundary.scala:91 BoundaryBeliefInput(weights: Map[Int, Map[BoundarySignal, Double]]),
story/nodes.scala:121 (BoundaryBelief.level), story/hierarchy.scala:11 (SegmentNode.level) and
:84 (descendantsAtLevel). The bare integer really does appear on both sides -- perceptual
evidence in features, structural containment in story.

1. A SINGLE Level WRAPPER IS REFUSED, AND IT WOULD BE WORSE THAN THE BARE Int. This is the part
of new-engineer's warning I want to generalise, because it is a defect class we do not have a
name for: TYPING A CONFLATED QUANTITY DOES NOT UN-CONFLATE IT, IT LAUNDERS IT. A mechanical
replacement of every `level: Int` with one `Level` would pass review, compile, gate green, and
preserve the exact scientific conflation under a name that now IMPLIES semantics it does not
have. The bare Int is at least honest: it advertises that it carries no meaning, so a reader
knows to go and find out. `Level` says the question has been settled. A partial fix that removes
the smell without removing the defect is the worst of the three states, and this one is
attractive precisely because it is a one-line-per-site change that looks like progress.

So: at least two NON-INTERCHANGEABLE coordinates, as proposed -- task-and-grain semantics for
perceptual evidence and its weights, versus hierarchy depth for resolved segment containment.
SegmentNode.level may stay structural depth under its own type, and must NOT become the public
grain vocabulary by convenience, which is the path of least resistance and therefore the one to
name in the ADR.

2. THE MAP KEY IS THE SHARPEST INSTANCE AND SHOULD LEAD THE ADR.
BoundaryBeliefInput.weights: Map[Int, Map[BoundarySignal, Double]] is not merely storing a level.
A MAP KEY IS A COMPARABILITY CLAIM: two entries under key 2 are asserted to be the same level,
by the data structure itself, with no code anywhere having decided that. Every other site can be
read as an untyped field awaiting a type. This one actively performs the conflation on every
lookup.

3. ATOMIC MIGRATION, AND HERE IS WHY THIS IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT WE DID ALL DAY. I have spent
today slicing a sweep into seven independent pieces and landing them one at a time, and that was
correct BECAUSE construction boundaries are per-type: closing fromProduct on Credence has no
bearing on whether it is closed on TextSpan, so a half-done sweep is simply a smaller done
sweep. THIS MIGRATION IS NOT LIKE THAT. One surviving Map[Int, _] or one un-migrated codec field
re-bridges the two coordinates for everything downstream, so a half-done migration is not a
smaller done migration -- it is an undone migration that LOOKS done, with a typed vocabulary
sitting on top of a live comparability bridge. Migrate BoundaryEvidence, BoundaryScore,
BoundaryBeliefInput keying, the story-side belief, codecs, laws and fixtures together or not at
all.

Nobody should read today's slicing pattern as the house style. It was right for a per-type
property and it is wrong here, and I would rather say that now than review a slice-1-of-6 proposal.

4. SEQUENCING UNCHANGED, now with a reason. No implementation bead. Freeze the multi-story
decision fixture, write the two-coordinate ADR, and only then choose names and wire shapes --
because the wire shape is where the atomicity requirement in 3 is either satisfied or silently
broken, and a name chosen before the coordinates are settled will be the name that gets
overloaded.

5. And per my Q1 ruling: if a story-side retained belief derives from perceptual evidence it
must PRESERVE the task-grain identity and the resolver or ledger receipt, never reconstruct
either from segment depth. Reconstructing a task-conditioned quantity from a structural one is
exactly how (B) would get recycled as gold for (A).
